headline_marked: [[Man jailed for 10 months]] due to name mix-up; High Court orders investigation
headline: Man jailed for 10 months due to name mix-up; High Court orders investigation
summary: A man named Md. Almas has been imprisoned for over 10 months in an arms case, claiming he is not the actual convict who was sentenced 22 years ago. The High Court has now ordered an investigation into the identity mix-up.
details: A man named Md. Almas has been languishing in jail for over 10 months, arrested in an arms case where the actual convict, also named Md. Almas, was sentenced 22 years ago. He claims he is a victim of mistaken identity due to a name similarity.

The original case involved an arms act, with Dhaka Metropolitan Special Tribunal-11 sentencing Md. Almas (father: Md. Khalil Ahmed, village: Dakshin Bahra, Dohar, Dhaka) to 10 years in prison on June 19, 2004. The verdict also mentioned the convict's current address as Ahmednagar, Paikpara, Mirpur.

The current inmate, Md. Almas, filed a writ petition with the High Court, asserting that he has been wrongly arrested and imprisoned in place of the actual convict. His petition states his name as Md. Almas, father Sheikh Khalil, village Sundaripara, Dohar, Dhaka.

Records show the case was filed on April 10, 2002, against Md. Almas (then 24) and Md. Nazmul Alam Mamun (then 22). The court sentenced Almas but he was absconding at the time of the verdict, leading to an arrest warrant. The current Almas states he was 16 years old when the case was filed in 2002, not 24.

The jailed Almas stated in his writ that he was previously arrested in 2018 for the same case due to the name similarity. He was released then on a bail bond, which acknowledged partial errors in the accused's name and address, and was handed over to his father's custody.

A certificate from the then-chairman of Kusumbati Union Parishad, dated February 22, 2018, confirmed that Md. Almas from Dakshin Bahra, son of Khalil Ahmed, was the absconding convict, and the local resident (Md. Almas, son of Sheikh Khalil) was not the actual accused. It also stated the convicted person sold his house and moved away about 25 years ago.
The current Almas (father Sheikh Khalil) was presented in court as the convicted person on November 5 last year, following a warrant issued on March 20, 2024. The court subsequently sent him to jail.

A police report suggests the case was filed against Almas while he lived in Bahra. His home was destroyed by river erosion in 2005 or 2006, after which he moved to Sundaripara (Kusumhati) village in the same Upazila and went into hiding. Police investigation, based on local inquiries, concluded there was no other person named Md. Almas, son of Sheikh Khalil alias Khalil Ahmed, in Dakshin Bahra.

The High Court bench of Justice JBM Hassan and Justice Aziz Ahmed Bhuiyan issued a rule and ordered an investigation into the identities of the petitioner Almas (currently in jail) and the convicted person. The Chief Judicial Magistrate of Dhaka has been tasked with overseeing the investigation, to be completed within 45 days.

The court also issued a rule asking why the arrest and detention of the petitioner should not be declared illegal and why he should not be compensated with BDT 5 crore. The matter is scheduled for further hearing on November 5.

headline: Lula's lead over Bolsonaro narrows ahead of Brazil vote, runoff likely
summary: A new poll shows President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's lead shrinking against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, indicating a potentially tight race and a strong possibility of a second-round vote.
details: A recent CNT/MDA poll reveals that Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's lead over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has narrowed significantly. This development comes just ahead of Sunday's first-round vote, suggesting a much tighter contest than previously anticipated.

In the first-round scenario, Lula is projected to receive 43.1 percent of voter support, while Bolsonaro trails with 38 percent. Other candidates, Augusto Cury, Ronaldo Caiado, and Renan Santos, garnered smaller percentages.

When considering only valid votes, excluding blank or void ballots, Lula's support stands at 47.8 percent against Bolsonaro's 42.1 percent. This indicates that neither candidate is likely to secure the over 50 percent needed to win outright in the first round.

If no candidate achieves a majority on Sunday, the two frontrunners will proceed to a runoff election scheduled for October 25. The poll also projected a close runoff, with Lula receiving 47.3 percent compared to Bolsonaro's 43.1 percent.

This represents a tightening from a previous survey where Lula led Senator Bolsonaro by a larger margin of 47.3 percent to 40 percent in a hypothetical runoff. The latest poll surveyed 2,007 people from September 30 to October 2, with a margin of error of 2.2 percentage points.
